subsystems.name: Subsurface radiolytic source
subsystems.role: natural radioactivity in rock splits pore water into hydrogen and oxidants, giving life a food source with no sunlight needed.
parts: fracture and pore networks that let gases migrate

subsystems.name: Chemical and isotopic signature
subsystems.role: the fingerprint that a hydrogen-fed ecosystem would leave behind.
parts: mineral alteration such as magnetite, sulfides and sulfates

subsystems.name: Laboratory and analogue studies
subsystems.role: establishes what is biological and what is merely chemistry.

subsystems.name: In-situ instruments
subsystems.role: measures gases and organics at the source, underground.
parts: shallow drills (on the order of 2 m)

subsystems.name: Orbital and remote sensing
subsystems.role: searches whole planets and moons for plumes and surface alteration.

subsystems.name: Modelling and transport
subsystems.role: connects an underground source to a signal that can actually be seen from outside.

buildSteps.title: Characterise analogue sites
buildSteps.detail: In deep mines and Precambrian shield rock on Earth, measure hydrogen flux, the resident microbial community and isotope ratios over several years.

buildSteps.title: Build a radiation-chemistry baseline
buildSteps.detail: Irradiate drill cores and synthetic rock-water mixtures in the lab, and combine measured uranium, thorium and potassium content with dose calculations to predict hydrogen production per cubic metre per year.

buildSteps.title: Catalogue abiotic false positives
buildSteps.detail: List every non-biological route to the same gases — serpentinisation, magmatic degassing, meteoritic organics, and contamination from the spacecraft itself.

buildSteps.title: Design the biosignature suite
buildSteps.detail: Decide that no single gas counts; require several independent signals — gases, isotopes and minerals — to agree before calling anything biological.

buildSteps.title: Test instruments in analogue boreholes
buildSteps.detail: Flight-qualify a drill and mass spectrometer by running them down terrestrial mine galleries and boreholes, far from clean-room conditions.

buildSteps.title: Fly remote-sensing instruments
buildSteps.detail: Put trace-gas and near-infrared spectrometers in orbit, and calibrate them against known abiotic sources on Earth and the Moon.

buildSteps.title: Acquire subsurface samples
buildSteps.detail: Drill into the radiolytic zone — the Rosalind Franklin rover's roughly 2 m drill is the deepest planned on Mars — or return samples for laboratory isotope work.

buildSteps.title: Confirm by replication
buildSteps.detail: Require the same result from independent instruments, independent sites and independent laboratories before treating it as a biosignature.

prerequisites.why: without it there is no way to predict how much hydrogen a given rock could supply.
mines and scientific drilling reach kilometres down on Earth, but planetary drilling has barely scratched the surface.
methane can be measured from orbit but very low levels remain contested, and no orbital instrument is dedicated to hydrogen.
isotopic fractionation is the strongest available discriminator between biological and abiotic gas.
the expected signals are faint, and hardware and humans can introduce similar organics.

pathway.milestone: terrestrial analogue work in deep mines and shield rock, plus orbital methane surveys and the hydrogen measured in the plume of Enceladus
pathway.unlocks: a working picture of what radiolytically fed life looks like and what it emits.

pathway.milestone: shallow subsurface sampling on Mars, and icy-moon flybys and orbiters arriving in the early 2030s
pathway.unlocks: measurements of the chemistry and radiation environment where the process is expected.

pathway.milestone: dedicated hydrogen and methane instruments, and laboratory study of returned samples
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a detected signal is not an abiotic or contamination artefact.

pathway.milestone: drilling or sub-ice access reaching the radiolytic zone itself
pathway.unlocks: the decisive test — sampling the habitat, not just its leaking gases.
